title: Check yourself: One Messages API, three front doors

questions.stem: A team moves a working direct-API request to Google Cloud and keeps the body unchanged. It is refused. Which changes does the page require?

options.text: Add an `anthropic-version` header and remove nothing else from the body
options.says: Ruled out because the version is passed "rather than as a header".

options.text: Keep the model in the payload and send the version as a request header
options.says: Ruled out because "`model` is not passed in the request body", and the version is "rather than as a header".

options.text: Move both the model and the version into the query string of the address
options.says: Ruled out because the model "is specified in the Google Cloud endpoint URL", which is the address path, not a query string.

options.text: Name the model in the address and carry the version in the payload
options.says: The page says "`model` is not passed in the request body" and that it "is specified in the Google Cloud endpoint URL", while `anthropic_version` goes "in the request body".

questions.stem: A developer calls Claude Opus 5.5 through Bedrock with the identifier `claude-opus-5-5` and gets an error. What fixes it?

options.text: Add the provider prefix so the name starts with anthropic
options.says: The page says "Model IDs in Claude in Amazon Bedrock carry an `anthropic.` provider prefix".

options.text: Use the dated name that the direct API shows, with no prefix at all
options.says: Ruled out because the Bedrock ids "carry an `anthropic.` provider prefix" and are not the direct API names.

options.text: Use the Vertex form of the name, with an at sign and a date after it
options.says: Ruled out because the at-sign form belongs to Google Cloud, where "`model` is not passed in the request body".

options.text: Send the name in a request header called x-model instead of the body
options.says: Ruled out because the model stays in the body on Bedrock, "the same request body shape as Anthropic's first-party API".

questions.stem: A security team wants no long-lived keys on developer laptops when calling Claude through Bedrock. Which path does the page favour?

options.text: A single shared access key stored with the source code of the project
options.says: Ruled out because the service role is the path "for the most secure, long-lived access", with "AWS-managed keys" and no shared key in the source.

options.text: Bearer tokens kept in each laptop's configuration file for daily use
options.says: Ruled out because bearer tokens are "(12-hour maximum, least preferred)".

options.text: A provisioned service role that the platform assumes for the caller
options.says: The page marks the service role as the recommended path: "Use a Bedrock service role with AWS-managed keys for the most secure, long-lived access".

options.text: An assumed role with a session that lasts for a full working week
options.says: Ruled out because an assumed role has "a 12-hour maximum session", not a week.
